speaker: NARRATOR
text: [storyteller, brisk] Montreal, the 1930s. A young researcher at McGill named Hans Selye is hunting for the thing that'll make his name: a brand-new hormone.

speaker: SELYE
text: [eager, muttering to himself, fast] If I inject the extract and the rats change, it's something new. It MUST be something new.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [amused] Every day he injects his rats with extract from cow ovaries. And, as the story is usually told, he is TERRIBLE at it.

speaker: SELYE
text: [offended] I am not terrible, I am— [gasps] No, no, no, no—!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [laughing, fast] He fumbles the injections. He drops the rats. They escape.

speaker: SELYE
text: [breathless, chasing, panicked] Come back—! Come back here—!

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [barely holding in a laugh] And Hans Selye ends up chasing them around the lab. With a broom.

speaker: YOU
text: [laughs] A broom?

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [laughs softly] A broom. [deadpan] For months.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [shift, quieter, serious] Then he opens the rats up. And there it is. Swollen adrenal glands. A shrunken immune system. Bleeding ulcers in the stomach.

speaker: SELYE
text: [hushed, thrilled, almost giggling] It worked. It WORKED.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: He'd found his hormone. [pause] [dry] Except he hadn't.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [explaining, steady] Because he also had a control group: rats he'd injected with nothing but salt water. Completely harmless.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [slowly] And they had the exact. Same. Damage.

speaker: YOU
text: [quietly] Wait — the salt water ones too?

speaker: SELYE
text: [quiet, deflated] That's not possible.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [gently, piecing it together] It wasn't the extract. It wasn't anything he injected. What every rat had in common was the EXPERIENCE. [quicker, listing] The needles, the dropping, the chasing, the broom.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [softly] Their bodies weren't reacting to a chemical. They were reacting to life going badly.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [brisk] So he tested it.

speaker: SELYE
text: [scribbling notes, muttering, faster each time] Cold — same. Exhaustion — same. Injury — [stunned] same.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Different ordeals. Same response. Every single time.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [informative, flowing] In 1936 he published it, a short letter in the journal Nature, which didn't even use the word "stress" yet. That came later.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But when it came, Selye reached for the engineering word. Pressure on a structure. Load on a frame.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [warm, a touch of awe] And he spent the rest of his life carrying it around the world.
